links.outcome: Guideline adherence, unsafe recommendations, and grading accuracy with structured (CARDS) vs simple prompts
links.effect: For GPT-4o and o3, structured prompts raised guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, cut unsafe recommendations from 16.7% to 0%, and raised grading accuracy from 0% to 100%. Llama models gained less.
links.quote: For some closed-source models (GPT-4o, o3), prompts structured in the CARDS style improved guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, eliminated unsafe recommendations (16.7% to 0%), and increased specific guideline grading accuracy from 0% to 100%.

links.outcome: LLM guideline adherence and unsafe thrombolysis recommendations by model
links.effect: Under simple prompts, some models made unsafe recommendations (16.7%). Llama-4-Scout and Llama-3.3-70B still had guideline adherence of 66.7% and unsafe recommendations of 33.3% with structured prompts.
links.quote: In contrast, other open-source models (Llama-4-Scout, Llama-3.3-70B) showed more modest gains: risk recognition improved (83.3% to 100%) and guideline grading accuracy increased (0% to 66.7%), while guideline adherence (66.7%) and unsafe recommendations (33.3%) persisted.
